question: Tell me about a time a major change occurred mid-project. How did you communicate with the customer and adjust the plan?

raiseTranscript.text: Tell me about a time a major change occurred mid-project. How did you communicate with the customer and adjust the plan?

We were building a reporting dashboard for a small client. Two weeks in, they asked to swap the data source from CSV to their new API. I updated my task list, checked with my mentor on the effort, then emailed the client a revised two-week timeline with the new scope. We delivered on the new date.
What did the customer say when you sent the update?
They appreciated the heads-up and the new date. My mentor later told me to always include options next time.

raiseNotes: Q: Tell me about a time a major change occurred mid-project. How did you communicate with the customer and adjust the plan?
Role: Junior dev on 4-week dashboard build
Situation: Client swapped CSV to API mid-sprint
Action: Checked effort with mentor, sent email with revised 2-week timeline
Outcome: Delivered on new date; customer thanked us
Quote: "My mentor later told me to always include options next time."
Follow-up: What did the customer say? - Appreciated the heads-up
junior.raiseFeedback: Raises the bar on Customer success is our success for a junior. The candidate owned the scope change at an individual level by confirming effort with a mentor before updating the customer. The story shows they adjusted their own plan and sent a clear timeline update. The follow-up reveals coachability when the mentor suggested adding options. Biggest strength is closing the loop with the customer instead of hiding the change.

raiseTranscript.text: Tell me about a time a major change occurred mid-project. How did you communicate with the customer and adjust the plan?

We were delivering a new analytics module for a key account when they changed their data retention policy. I pulled the cross-team leads, modeled the new storage costs, then ran a joint call with the customer to present two options: reduced scope or four-week extension. We chose the extension and hit the revised date with no extra cost to them.
How did you get the other teams aligned?
I scheduled a 30-minute working session and had each team bring their delta in writing before we talked to the customer.

raiseNotes: Q: Tell me about a time a major change occurred mid-project. How did you communicate with the customer and adjust the plan?

Situation: Customer changed data retention policy mid-delivery

Outcome: Four-week extension chosen; delivered on time with no extra cost

senior.raiseFeedback: Raises the bar on Customer success is our success for a senior. The candidate drove cross-team alignment and gave the customer clear trade-off options instead of a single revised plan. The story includes measurable impact (on-time delivery, no extra cost) and shows influence without authority by getting written input from teams. Biggest strength is turning a policy change into a controlled negotiation that protected the customer relationship.

raiseTranscript.text: Tell me about a time a major change occurred mid-project. How did you communicate with the customer and adjust the plan?

Our largest enterprise customer announced they were moving to a new cloud provider, affecting a multi-year migration program. I convened the account, product, and finance leads, then proposed a phased transition plan that protected their existing SLAs while we rebuilt the pipeline. I personally briefed their CTO on the risks and the two-year investment required from us. We kept the account and signed a renewal.
What trade-offs did you present internally?
We modeled a 15% margin hit if we accelerated versus spreading the work and accepting a one-quarter delay on another initiative.

Biggest strength is treating the change as a portfolio-level decision rather than a single-project adjustment.
